items.title: CSV export silently overwrites existing companion files

findings.title: CSV export silently overwrites existing companion files
findings.explanation: The save dialog in PictologicsSlicer.py:2700-2715 only selects and confirms the main CSV. The writer at lines 3849-3870 also generates <stem>.provenance.json and <stem>_catalog.csv, and exports.py:55-58 replaces every destination. Thus exporting a new features.csv can silently destroy an unrelated existing features_catalog.csv or features.provenance.json, even when the main CSV did not exist. The temporary backups are removed after success.
findings.suggestion: Before writing, enumerate all destinations and explicitly confirm every existing file that will be replaced, or refuse collisions and let the user select another name.

claude.reason: Verified. PictologicsSlicer.py:2700-2715 only shows the OS save dialog for the main file. writeSet (3849-3871) also writes <stem>.provenance.json and <stem>_catalog.csv, and exports.py:55-58 os.replace()s every destination after backing it up to a temp dir that is removed on success. An unrelated file with a matching name is therefore overwritten with no prompt. The companion names are derived from the chosen stem, though, and the code comment at 3862-3863 says replacing an older catalog is intentional. It also fails safe for symlinks and directories (exports.py:46-47) and rolls back on error. This is a small UX/data-loss gap that needs a coincidentally named file. It is not a concrete path to serious harm, so it is not blocking.

gpt.reason: PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py:2700-2715 selects only the main filename and checks that path, not its companions; lines 3849-3873 create both companions, including `dictionaryPath = stagedPath.with_name(f"{stagedPath.stem}_catalog.csv")`. PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsLib/exports.py:44-57 backs up any existing targets then executes `os.replace(source, target)` for each; lines 76-81 delete the staging directory on success. Thus even a new features.csv can silently destroy an unrelated existing features_catalog.csv or features.provenance.json. The user guide, docs/user-guide.md:51-57, describes companion creation but does not provide collision confirmation. Confirm all existing destinations before publication.

gemini.reason: Verified in PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py:2700-2715 (`onExport` only checks overwrite confirmation for the main CSV path via `QFileDialog.getSaveFileName` or `path.with_suffix(".csv").exists()`), PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py:3849-3873 (`writeSet` always generates `<stem>.provenance.json` and `<stem>_catalog.csv` alongside `<stem>.csv` and notes in line 3862-3863: "Always write it, so that an empty catalog replaces the one of an older export"), and PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsLib/exports.py:44-58 (`export_file_set` calls `os.replace(source, target)` for every file in the set). While the code does replace existing `<stem>.provenance.json` and `<stem>_catalog.csv` without separate prompts if `<stem>.csv` didn't exist, these are tightly named sidecar files (`<stem>.provenance.json` and `<stem>_catalog.csv`) in a user-selected save directory during an explicit export action. Prompting before overwriting pre-existing sidecars when the main file doesn't exist would be a nice minor UX improvement, not a blocking safety issue.

items.title: Configuration validation blocks the Slicer GUI

findings.title: Configuration validation blocks the Slicer GUI
findings.explanation: The Validate handler calls this method directly on the GUI thread (lines 1825-1829). If the helper is slow or stuck, communicate blocks the event loop for up to five minutes; the timeout limits the duration but does not keep the UI responsive.
findings.suggestion: Run the check asynchronously or poll the process while reporting progress and supporting cancellation.

items.title: Multiple large derivative branding assets committed to the source repository

findings.title: Multiple large derivative branding assets committed to the source repository
findings.evidence:
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-master-1254.png  (1675535 bytes, binary)
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-master-1254.webp  (1144018 bytes, binary)
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-vector-render-4096.png  (1223228 bytes, binary)
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-white-1254.jpg  (597284 bytes, binary)
findings.explanation: The repository includes 22 derivative branding files in `assets/branding/pictologics/` (including a ~2 MB `.icns`, ~2 MB `.tiff`, ~1.7 MB master PNG, ~1.2 MB 4096px PNG, ~1.1 MB `.eps`, ~1.1 MB `.webp`, ~1.1 MB 1024px PNG, and ~0.9 MB `.svg`), totaling ~13 MB in the git checkout. While CMake properly excludes these from the built Slicer extension archive, committing multiple multi-megabyte master and print-format derivatives increases repository clone size for the Extensions Index build system and contributors.
findings.suggestion: Consider keeping only the catalog/module PNG icons and the master source (or generating derivatives on demand with `scripts/export_branding_assets.py`) to keep the git repository lightweight.

gpt.reason: The verified unconfirmed companion-file overwrite in D1 is a concrete path to user data loss, so safety is blocking rather than ok or unknown: PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py:3849-3873 generates companions and PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsLib/exports.py:55-57 calls `os.replace(source, target)`. I also checked the export dialog at PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py:2691-2742 and searched the GUI and CLI sources for network, process-execution, deserialization and deletion APIs; this is not a complete audit. The downloaded Pictologics package and exact repository revision were not independently verified.

gemini.reason: The extension performs local radiomics feature extraction and export using staged atomic writes (`PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsLib/exports.py:19-81`, `PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py:3849-3874`), checks for symlinks/non-files before writing (`exports.py:46-47`), and has no malicious behavior, hidden network calls, or unsafe deserialization. Writing the companion `<stem>.provenance.json` and `<stem>_catalog.csv` files during a user-initiated CSV export is minor at most and does not warrant a blocking safety rating.
